speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a low-grade fever, an itchy rash, and joint pain that started after antibiotic treatment; can you tell me exactly which antibiotic you were prescribed?

Also, when did these symptoms begin relative to your last dose, and how would you describe the appearance of the rash?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amoxicillin-induced serum sickness-like reaction.

Given the classic presentation of fever, itchy rash starting in flexural areas (antecubital/popliteal fossae), and joint pain following amoxicillin use for sinusitis in an 8-year-old, the clinical picture strongly suggests a serum sickness-like reaction rather than a simple drug allergy or viral exanthem. Would you like me to confirm this with a complete blood count (CBC) showing eosinophilia or order specific serum IgE testing before finalizing the treatment plan?
